title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers to understand churn dynamics. The overall churn rate is 37.7%. Key drivers include contract type, with monthly subscribers showing significantly higher churn, and a distinct at-risk segment characterized by high support ticket volume and low satisfaction. Lifetime value scales substantially with plan tier.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers. The overall churn rate is 37.7%, and the average monthly fee is $42.11.
Churn rates are similar across plans, ranging from 36.6% (Premium) to 38.9% (Basic). Basic plan customers have the highest churn rate.
Churn rates have remained relatively stable across signup cohorts from 2021 to 2023 (around 37%), with a slight increase to 39.8% in the 2024 cohort.
Monthly contract customers churn at a rate of 48.3%, which is 121.1% higher than the 21.9% rate for Annual contract customers.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers with high support tickets (>=5) and low satisfaction (<=2) exhibits a churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0) with a standard deviation of 13.2 months. Average satisfaction is 3.42, with 27 missing scores.
Average Lifetime Value (LTV) is highest for Premium customers ($1,816.78), followed by Standard ($868.83) and Basic ($463.46). Premium LTV is 292.0% higher than Basic LTV.

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not reflect real-time changes.
Satisfaction scores were missing for 27 customers, potentially biasing the average satisfaction metric.
Causality cannot be inferred; observed associations (e.g., between contract type and churn) may be influenced by unobserved factors.
conclusion: To reduce churn, the business should prioritize converting monthly subscribers to annual contracts and address the high-churn at-risk segment through targeted retention strategies. The significant LTV gap between Basic and Premium plans suggests that upselling initiatives could drive substantial revenue growth.
